title: Monsoon and Provision
premise: Rafael Nystrom, a salvage diver drifting upriver on a leaking boat, finds a chest stamped with the seal of a nation that no longer exists — and with it a ledger naming descendants owed an inheritance that powerful men have spent decades burying. Hunted by a shipping magnate's private enforcers who want the chest silenced, Rafael is forced to stop running for the first time in years, sheltering through the monsoon in a river town whose people have their own grievances against the magnate. With help from Odile, a ferry pilot with her own claim to justice, Rafael must decide whether to sell the inheritance or deliver it, culminating in a storm-lit confrontation at the magnate's river depot where the chest's contents are finally read aloud to the town. The dry season ends with the inheritance distributed, the enforcers exposed, and Rafael choosing, for once, to stay.
about_author: Kestrel Quintana is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent six years charting wrecks along contested river deltas before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who belong to water more than to any country.

chapters.title: The Navy Won't Discuss It
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Diving a restricted wreck site, Rafael salvages what the navy leaves behind, selling scrap to survive another week. A patrol boat runs them off without explanation, deepening the sense that some wrecks are secrets, not tragedies. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness; Rafael plans to move on before anyone learns their name.

chapters.title: Leaking at the Seams
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The boat takes on water faster than the bilge pump can manage, forcing Rafael into a shanty repair yard where the mechanic warns the monsoon is weeks early. Broke after paying for patches, Rafael takes one last dive job upriver. Emotional beat: the cost of never stopping made literal in rotting wood.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Up
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Diving a drowned ferry crossing, Rafael's light catches a steel chest wedged in the hull, stamped with the seal of Vessany — a nation dissolved forty years ago. Hauling it aboard nearly costs them their air line. Emotional beat: awe curdling quickly into dread as Rafael realizes the wreck was scuttled, not sunk.

chapters.title: A Dead Nation's Seal
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, opening the chest: sealed documents, a brass ledger of names and holdings, and letters never delivered. The last entry names a whole town's worth of heirs. That night a fast boat with no lights sweeps past, searching. Emotional beat: wonder giving way to the old instinct to run — but the boat won't make it far.

chapters.title: Men Who Ask Politely
chapters.summary: Two enforcers from Corvane Shipping board Rafael's boat at a fuel dock, polite and thorough, asking about 'recovered artifacts.' Rafael lies well enough to buy hours, not days. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into calculation; Rafael understands these men don't retrieve things, they erase them.

chapters.title: Odile Ferries Strangers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ferry pilot Odile Marchand spots Rafael's listing boat and tows them into her home port of Brasse-Lune ahead of the first real storm. She recognizes the Vessany seal instantly — her grandmother's name is in stories about it. Emotional beat: wary hospitality between two people who've both learned not to trust.

chapters.title: Brasse-Lune in the Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The monsoon arrives in earnest, trapping Rafael in a town that runs on gossip and grudge. Odile introduces Rafael to the tavern keeper, the schoolteacher, the dockhand — all descendants, unknowingly, of the ledger's names. Emotional beat: belonging offered casually, which frightens Rafael more than the enforcers do.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Names
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Reading the ledger by lamplight with Odile, they match names to living townspeople: land titles, fishing rights, a warehouse, all seized by Corvane's founder when Vessany collapsed. Emotional beat: the slow burn of injustice becoming personal; this isn't treasure, it's theft with paperwork.

chapters.title: Running Costs More
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael tries to leave alone — sell the chest downriver and vanish — but the patched hull fails in open current and Odile hauls them back a second time. Shamed and soaked, Rafael admits why they keep moving: a warrant from an old job, a family that stopped writing. Emotional beat: the confession Rafael has avoided for years.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Stories
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile shares her grandmother's accounts of the Vessany dissolution — neighbors disappeared, deeds burned, a resistance that smuggled records into the river wrecks. The chest was meant to be found someday. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; Odile claims her stake in the fight.

chapters.title: Corvane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A Corvane lawyer arrives openly now, offering Rafael money and a clean record for the chest. The warrant that haunts Rafael would simply... disappear. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare; Rafael realizes the offer is proof of how much the ledger is worth — and how little Rafael is trusted to matter.

chapters.title: The Town Decides It Isn't Afraid
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Against Odile's caution, the schoolteacher reads selected ledger entries aloud in the tavern. Old resentments catch fire; the town votes, informally, to stand together. Emotional beat: collective courage rising, with Rafael watching from the doorway, unsure they've earned a place in it.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Corvane stops being polite: enforcers cut mooring lines and torch a skiff as warning. In the chaos Rafael dives to hide the chest in the flooded quarry, nearly drowning when a line snags. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused; there is no version of leaving anymore.

chapters.title: Allies in Odd Places
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile recruits the mechanic, a retired harbor master, and a Corvane deckhand with a conscience, building a plan to move the chest during the storm's worst night, when patrols hunker down. Emotional beat: improvised family forming around a shared cause.

chapters.title: The Warrant Surfacing
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The lawyer plays his card publicly: Rafael's old warrant, posters on every post. The town's reaction splits — some want Rafael gone before Corvane burns everything. Emotional beat: Rafael's deepest fear realized; belonging tested at its weakest seam.

chapters.title: What Rafael Would Take Back
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile finds Rafael packing at dawn and forces the full story out: the botched salvage job, the man hurt, the years of paying a debt Corvane itself helped create — the injured man was a whistleblower they buried. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered not as absolution but as invitation to stay and finish something.

chapters.title: Storm's Worst Night
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The team moves the chest by ferry through whiteout rain while enforcers sweep the quarry. A near-collision, a silent transfer under a bridge, Odile flying the ferry blind through channels she knows by heart. Emotional beat: trust executed at speed; Rafael realizes they're no longer working alone.

chapters.title: The Depot at Low Water
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The plan turns bolder: deliver the ledger to the regional magistrate at Corvane's own river depot, where the dry-season cargo audit will force officials on record. Rafael infiltrates the depot as a contract diver. Emotional beat: nerve stretched thin; the trap they're walking into could close either way.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. Cornered in the depot office, Rafael and Odile stall until the magistrate and gathered townspeople arrive; the ledger is read aloud — names, seizures, signatures, including Corvane's founder and the navy officer who scuttled the ferry. Enforcers move, the storm knocks the power out, and the town holds the line in the dark. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, enforced by witnesses rather than warrants.

chapters.title: After the Water Goes Down
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The magistrate opens an inquiry; Corvane's local operations freeze; the warrant against Rafael is quietly withdrawn as leverage collapses. The town begins filing inheritance claims, arguing cheerfully over acreage and boats. Emotional beat: exhausted, unglamorous victory; the ordinary work of getting what was taken back.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael repairs the boat properly this time — new planking, honest caulking — and stocks it not for escape but for work: running salvage and supply runs for the town's claims. Emotional beat: quiet transformation; provision meaning both supplies and providing for others.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season, Next Year
chapters.summary: Dual POV, closing chapter. One year later, the first rains arrive and Rafael doesn't leave. Odile and Rafael take the ferry out to the old wreck to lay flowers for the ferry's dead, then turn home to a lit harbor. Emotional beat: belonging chosen and kept; the story ends not with departure but with arrival.
